trails.title: DJB: from tender eligibility to the disputed money trail
trails.question: What was actually paid, who allegedly received it, and which document would establish the next beneficiary?
trails.conclusion: Original 2026 orders advance the trace to an ECIR-asserted ₹24,74,71,376 release and precise alleged bank/cash components. Actual recipient schedules, company distributions and political-pool allocation remain untraced; equivalent-value attachment is not recovery proof.
trails.sourceStatus: Two original judicial orders; two official ED releases from the same agency origin; dated company disclosure; a retained bail mirror and a reported AAP response. Alleged payments remain attributed and contested.
limitations: One bounded contract case, not all Delhi Jal Board expenditure.
No original bank statement or executed subcontract obtained.
Court/agency names, units and cost revisions are explicitly retained; no silent corrections or current ownership inference.
No minister or family recipient inferred from association.

hops.summary: NBCC Faridabad-project certificates became the eligibility bridge into a DJB bid. Tribunal describes an adverse March 2018 inspection and a subsequent favourable note-sheet; investigate sign-offs and overwritten versions.
hops.dateBasis: No exact underlying transfer date published in retained source; source/decision dates are shown separately.
hops.response: Defence disputes proceeds/GST, predicate offence and evidentiary reliability. Procedural outcomes do not determine guilt.
alternatives: Lawful expenditure, tax and timing differences need source-led reconciliation; an agency assertion does not establish the actual bank path.

hypotheses.question: Did the eligibility file admit an unqualified bidder, or omit valid corroboration?
hypotheses.observation: The tribunal recites an adverse inspection, three performance certificates, an unsigned negative draft and a later favourable note-sheet.
hypotheses.disconfirmationTest: A valid contemporaneous completion/SCADA demonstration meeting NIT 22 and an authenticated approval trail would weaken the false-eligibility theory.
hypotheses.documentHolder: DJB tender branch; NBCC project office; court exhibits

hypotheses.question: Do the alleged cash and bank allocations survive transaction-level corroboration?
hypotheses.observation: The court container reproduces exact amounts, but no original bank statement, Excel workbook or witness cross-examination was obtained.
expectedDocumentaryFootprints: Cash delivery witnesses independent of disputed statements
hypotheses.disconfirmationTest: Reconcile every questioned withdrawal/purchase against lawful supplier delivery, tax, work and the actual recipient; exclude retracted or uncorroborated entries rather than assuming they prove cash handovers.
hypotheses.documentHolder: Trial court permitted exhibits; ED; subcontract finance

hypotheses.question: Who, if anyone, actually received the alleged political-funding portion?
hypotheses.observation: The agency combines DJB officials and AAP in ₹2 crore; no recipient split or named minister is supplied.
expectedDocumentaryFootprints: Party-finance entry matched to actual payer
hypotheses.disconfirmationTest: Find a matched receipt/debit chain or a court-tested recipient witness; a missing party-ledger entry alone neither proves clandestine receipt nor refutes an alleged cash transfer.
neededRecords: Dated receipts and fund collector testimony
limitations: No party office, family tie or timing-only quid-pro-quo inference.

hypotheses.question: Did retained company funds reach owners or lawful project creditors?
hypotheses.observation: Historical ownership is known; no distribution record connects the ₹5,80,27,191 alleged company retention to those shareholders.
hypotheses.disconfirmationTest: Show lawful work liabilities, ordinary expense receipts or clean restrictions on distributions; only matched disbursements can establish personal benefit, not percentage ownership.
hypotheses.documentHolder: NKG finance/company secretary; MCA filings; trial court
limitations: Ownership class/date limited to 31 March 2020; no current ultimate-owner proof.

hypotheses.question: Can the work-cost allegation withstand a like-for-like scope comparison?
hypotheses.observation: ED public estimates shift from ₹17 crore in February to ₹14 crore in April; the award includes operation/maintenance, while scope/tax periods are not reconciled.
expectedDocumentaryFootprints: BOQ unit prices and measurement book
hypotheses.disconfirmationTest: Recompute actual executed work including legitimate GST, O&M, mobilization/retention and timing on a consistent basis; if the difference disappears, the inflation inference weakens.
hypotheses.documentHolder: DJB engineer and finance; ED valuation record
